To better understand the potential lighting effects in the two cities, the researchers again developed separate models for daytime with LED (Table 17), nighttime before LED conversion (Table 18), and daytime before LED conversion (Table 19). Note that SAS could not find a global optimization of the mixed-effect negative binomial model for the three additional scenarios and therefore fixed-effect models were used. The models showed that Cambridge had significantly more crashes during daytime after the LED conversion and during nighttime (after 10:00 p.m.) before the LED conversion. In the after LED daytime model, the parameter estimate was positive, indicating more daytime crashes in Cambridge compared to Somerville when controlling all other variables after the LED conversion. In the before LED nighttime model, the parameter estimate was negative, indicating fewer nighttime crashes in the city compared to Somerville when controlling all other variables.
